recap.text: Carl opens his Silver Earth box, the incentive for choosing an Earth class, and finds two random items and a Hobby potion. The first is a three-inch cactus in a clay pot, covered in yellow spikes, its $3.99 Home Depot tag still on. The second is a shrink-wrapped pack of eighteen westerns. Unlike Donut's candle and cat tree, these were not deliberate. Carl wonders why the cactus was chosen, sighs, and puts it into his inventory.

Carl and Donut learn that Li Na has cast a dread trap on his cactus, and Rosetta produces it glowing blue. One flower means she is safe, three mean alive but not safe, and dust means she died. Zhang points the pet carrier at Li Na and presses the button, and the white cleaner bot Suckira carries it off without a beep. A single flower blooms.

beats.headline: Three ninety-nine at Home Depot
beats.text: Carl's own Silver Earth box, the incentive for choosing an Earth class, holds two random items and a Hobby potion. The first is a small cactus plant in a clay pot, short and squat, about three inches tall and covered in yellow spikes, with the price tag still on the pot: $3.99, from a Home Depot. The second is a shrink-wrapped pack of eighteen westerns. Donut's gifts were deliberate, a candle and a cat tree. Carl examines the cactus, wondering why they chose it for him, sighs, and puts it into his inventory.
beats.gist: Carl's Earth box holds a three-inch cactus with a $3.99 Home Depot tag, and he pockets it.

beats.headline: A dread for a signal
beats.text: Donut tells Carl that Li Na has cast some gooey dread thing on his cactus. Rosetta produces it, glowing blue: a dread trap, Deadly bloom, which normally blooms when someone comes near and releases a paralysing spore. Carl knows it: it came from picking an Earth class, and it was in his room until Samantha put it out for not matching the new rug. Its state will report Li Na. Glowing, she is alive in the dungeon. Blooming and spreading spores but unlit, she has left the game. Dust, she died inside. Prepotente leans in and tells them to keep it somewhere safe: what if she is trapped in the bot? Then the glow will fail over several days. One flower, still glowing, means come. Three means alive but not safe.
beats.gist: Donut says Li Na cursed Carl's cactus; Rosetta produces a glowing dread trap.

beats.headline: Everyone looks at the cactus
beats.text: Zhang, who has to be the one, points the pet carrier at Li Na and presses the button, and she is inside it. The white cleaner bot Suckira picks the carrier up and it is gone without so much as a beep. Nothing happens. Everyone turns to the cactus. So far there is no change. The one thing they do not want is for it to activate and then turn to dust, which would mean she is dead.
beats.gist: Zhang sends Li Na into the pet carrier, Suckira carries it off, and the cactus has not changed.

beats.headline: A single flower
beats.text: Carl has just read the reward for a finished quest and sighed that they need to get to work when Mordecai's message comes in. A single flower has just bloomed on the cactus. Donut gasps. It worked. One flower is the code for Li Na having made it to the Pineapple Cabaret, and for it being safe to bring the others the same way.
beats.gist: Li Na's cactus blooms a single flower, telling Carl and Donut she reached the Pineapple Cabaret safely.

beats.headline: The only one that talks
beats.text: Imani reports 227 crawlers sent to the Pineapple Cabaret, not counting Li Na, and Mordecai reports the cactus steady, glowing with a single bloom. The druid Ronit has worked out something simpler for the rest: a small potted plant for each of them, tied to that crawler's life, wilting or turning to dust if they die and blooming if they escape. Mordecai had to build a glass terrarium for the lot because the sluggalos were eyeing them. Li Na's dread cactus is the only one with the complicated messaging system.
beats.gist: Imani counts 227 crawlers sent to the Pineapple Cabaret, and Ronit gives each a potted plant.
